column13: 23 Aug strike (31 SBD + 5 of 6 TBF) landed at Henderson Field because the convoy was not found. 36 = 31 + 5 by my count. Launch about 1510; ONI times zone -11.5. Next day returned to Saratoga about 1130 less two SBD forced back to the island field.

column6: Not a pilot, crewman, or plane of the Saratoga attack group was lost
column13: 24 Aug Saratoga strike on Ryujo (30 SBD + 8 TBF; 29 SBD + 7 TBF reached the target). None lost to any cause. All but one landed Saratoga, the other on Enterprise; landed after sunset, at least 18 by about 1845.

column6: Two of the five planes did not return to the ship, the pilot and crew of one being located on the 28th safe on San Cristobal Island. The other plane presumably was shot down
column13: Second small strike (2 SBD + 5 TBF) at about 1708 on the cruiser force: 2 TBF of VT-8 lost, one crew found on San Cristobal on the 28th, the other 'presumably shot down'. Fuel not stated as the cause.

column6: The 11 SBD's ... landed just after dark on Guadalcanal
column13: 11 SBD of the 1708 strike (Caldwell) landed at Henderson Field; they stayed for weeks with VMS-232. The cv6 report says about 2100. Alternative to landing ashore had been offered at launch.

column6: the other four landed safely on the Saratoga about 2200
column13: 4 of the 7 TBF of the 1708 strike landed on Saratoga; they had jettisoned torpedoes to lighten the planes; 'The amount of gasoline with which the TBF's landed aboard varied between 4 and 40 gallons'. One TBF forced back by landing gear failure; 1 crashed into the barrier landing on Enterprise. ONI accounts for 6 of the 7.

column6: one crashed into the barrier while landing on the Enterprise
column13: TBF of the 1708 strike, crash on night return (the cv6 report says the second plane landing, windshield oiled, hit No. 2 crane at about 2158). Landing crash, not fuel.

column6: Water Landings (out of fuel): 1 VF, 2 VSB, 2 VTB
column13: Enterprise air group, 24 Aug, all causes of fuel exhaustion; not split by flight (search flight of 23 planes returned about 1715 and stayed aloft until the Japanese attack ended; the 1708 strike). Also 'missing (probably shot down)' 2 VF, 1 VTB and 'damaged, expended' 1 VF, 1 VTB.

column6: Several of our scouts exchanged shots with enemy planes ... Four were forced down, the pilots and crews of three being rescued by destroyers. The fourth plane landed on Stewart Island
column13: Planes of the 1315 search of 23 aircraft (250-mile sectors); cause 'forced down' not given (combat damage or fuel). Probably overlap with the 5 fuel water landings in the cv6 report; do not add the two rows.

column6: One torpedo plane failed to rendezvous ... became lost, ran out of fuel, and landed in the water
column13: 4 May Tulagi strikes; one TBD of the first group lost for fuel. Distance to Tulagi not stated.

column6: With the exception of the two SBD's shot down, the entire Lexington group had returned
column13: 7 May strike on Shoho: Lt Allen shot down; second SBD (Quigley) forced landing on Rossel Island, crew rescued by Australians. No fuel loss recorded. Lexington planes landed by about 1345.

column6: The missing plane was last seen ... when it broke off to attack an enemy plane
column13: 7 May: 1 SBD missing. No fuel loss recorded.

column6: One of our torpedo planes also was forced down and lost because of running out of gas
column13: 8 May strike on Shokaku/Zuikaku; TBD.

column6: Enemy fighters or fuel shortage accounted for all but one of our attacking scouts, and two of our fighters
column13: 8 May: 3 of the 4 attacking scouts (Ault's section) and 2 fighters; ONI does not split fighter and fuel loss. Count 3 + 2 by my reading; Ault was lost after being 'on his own', unable to find the carriers or be picked up by radar. Seven TBD arrived so short of fuel they were fired on by the Yorktown. Last plane landed about 1400.

column6: made a crash landing, striking the island structure ... the SBD was a wreck and was pushed over the side
column13: 8 May return: SBD of Lt Moan, crew survived. Wreck jettisoned. Landing crash, not fuel.

column6: seven torpedo bombers and one dive bomber ... another torpedo bomber (which later crashed)
column13: Dusk strike of 7 May (12 D3A + 15 B5N): 8 shot down by US CAP + 1 crashed afterwards, as the page gives it; 18 survivors, 'all were recovered by 22:00'. Losses in the night landing not stated on the page. Source: Wikipedia, notes not read. These are losses as the page states them, not US claims.

column6: None of Fighting 8 which went with the attack group returned to the ship. They remained with the VSB until forced to head for Midway due to lack of gas ... assumed to have landed in the water
column13: 4 June 0700 strike: all 10 F4F of VF-8 lost for fuel (Hornet report: 5 pilots rescued; ONI: 8 rescued). Count 10 from the same report (10 VF sent). Distance 155 mi.

column6: Thirteen planes of Bombing 8 landed at Midway due to lack of gas; two of these ran out of gas and landed in the Lagoon
column13: 4 June: 2 SBD ditched in Midway lagoon out of gas (ONI agrees: 'Thirteen reached Midway, where 2 landed in the lagoon').

column6: Thirteen planes of Bombing 8 landed at Midway due to lack of gas
column13: Includes the 2 that ditched in the lagoon; the other 11 were gassed, sent to attack and returned to Hornet 1727.

column6: All planes returned with the exception of one which landed in the water near the Enterprise due to fuel exhaustion
column13: 5 June strike of 26 SBD at 278 mi: 1 water landing out of fuel at night, crew picked up by Aylwin; 1 more landed out of fuel in the arresting gear (undamaged).

column13: Enterprise 8 TBF at 0900: 4 survived the attack, 2 landed on Enterprise 1425, 2 ran out of gas and made water landings. Fighters landed with 'none more than 18 gallons' (Hornet-wave fighters).
